About Event

Build what a single model cannot.
The next generation of AI products will not come from picking one model. It will come from knowing which models, agents, and modalities to bring together for a real task, then making the system work.
With the release of "system one" models like Jev that enable fast tool calling and model selection, developers have the ability to use multiple models that may generate different modalities of output such as video, audio, image, or classifier, to build applications that were previously difficult, expensive, and slow.
For SF Tech Week, BuilderBase, Actual AI, Women in AI, and AI Collective are bringing builders together at Frontier Tower for a full day of building, testing, and live demos.
The challenge
Build an AI product that becomes more useful because it combines more than one model, provider, agent, or modality. Use the right system for each job: reasoning, code, vision, voice, long context, fast inference, or whatever your product needs. Put them together with intelligent routing that can choose models based on modality, speed, and cost to achieve a goal.
Build something a real person would use. By the end of the day, show what it does, why one model would not have been enough, and what the combination unlocks.
Who should join
Engineers, AI practitioners, designers, and technical founders who want to build something real in a day. No prior hackathon experience required. Bring a laptop, a problem you care about, or the willingness to join a team and start building.
Sponsors
Anbaric
Anbaric builds workflows that combine human steps, agentic steps and coded steps; we don't believe in a world where humans are replaced by AI, but, rather, the AI unlocks human time and creativity by automating boring admin that fills our days.
Base44
Base44 is a no-code AI development platform that turns builders' ideas into fully functional apps and websites — no coding required.
Actual AI
Actual AI manages Architectural Decision Records (ADRs) in your codebase to ensure your agent writes the right code first time, no matter how large the codebase.
Prelint
Your AI makes decisions. Prelint keeps every decision reviewed, recorded, and traceable. Every pull request gets a 20-second decision review.
Swytchcode
Legacy APIs and AI agents don't blend. Swytchcode gives agents the implementation knowledge these APIs never documented, then governs every action that runs.
Community Partners
Women in AI
Women in AI connects, empowers, and elevates female founders, investors, and engineers shaping the future of artificial intelligence. Through community, mentorship, and global events, we’re building a more inclusive AI ecosystem where women lead and innovate.

This event is part of #SFTechWeek.

About Event

Car AI Navigation Hackathon

Challenge: We have a mini city road with lanes, intersection and traffic signs. Your job is to use AI and a small autonomous car like the Donkeycar or equivalent (typically 1/16th scale or smaller RC car with a Raspberry Pi or equivalent and a camera controlling it) to navigate the "city", obeying signs and making it from one side to the other in the fastest time.

You must bring your own car, which should be ready to run, with compute and camera already onboard and working. The objective of the hackathon is to add AI "city" navigation to it.

You can use onboard AI, AI on your laptop via Wifi or AI in the cloud to help with the navigation. Think creatively about what kind of AI to use and what's the fastest way to do it!

This is not an event for spectators, nor will cars be provided to those who arrive without one. This is a hackathon, not a regular race. Come ready to hack!

About Event

🛑 The best teacher a student ever has is about to be an AI. Build it.
One-on-one tutoring is the highest-leverage intervention in education. Bloom's 2-sigma problem, 30 years unsolved because good tutors do not scale. AI changes that. What used to cost $80 an hour with a Stanford grad student now runs at $0.03 per student per session.
But the model is not the product. The tutor is. Which subjects. Which pedagogy. Which feedback loops. Which trust signals. Which handoffs to a real teacher when the AI hits its limits.
This weekend we build the tutors that actually teach, not just answer.
🛠️ Join our Discord for credits, team formation, and support: Join Discord Server — 1-2 Builders per team

Build an Zero Human startup powered by a team of AI agents. Phase 1 is the foundation; Phase 2 is where you turn it into a functioning company.

Phase 1 — Build Day
In Person | 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM
Build 3 to 5 specialized AI agents across areas such as:
Product

Research

GTM

Sales

Marketing

Strategy

Your agents should work together through real workflows, not operate as standalone chatbots.
10:00 – 11:00 | Kickoff & Sponsor Demos
Challenge briefing

Sponsor tool demos

Team setup and Q&A

11:00 – 4:00 | Build Sprint
Build the foundation of your startup:
Identify and validate a problem

Build a simple working MVP

Create your initial AI agents

Define your business model and GTM

Prepare your demo and pitch

4:00 – 4:30 | Judging
Demo your startup and pitch to judges.
Phase 1 prizes are awarded after judging.
Completion of Phase 1 is required to continue to Phase 2.
Phase 2 — Build the Zero Human Company
October 7–11 | Online + In Person
Take your Phase 1 MVP and turn it into a functioning AI-native startup. You can build more then 5 agents now.
During Phase 2:
Build and connect your AI organization

Improve the product

Launch and test with users

Execute your GTM strategy

Collect feedback and iterate

Prepare an investor-ready pitch

October 11 — Final Demos & Review
Teams may present in person at participating locations for final demos and judging.
Final judging will consider the product, AI organization, execution, validation, GTM, traction, and final pitch.
Phase 2 has its own prizes and awards.

Phase 1: Idea → Validation → Simple MVP → Initial AI Team
Phase 2: MVP → 5+ AI Agents → Working AI Organization → Users → Investor Pitch
Sponsors & Tools
Kylon
Kylon helps you create AI agents that can run business processes. You can turn workflows into agents that understand tasks, use tools, and take actions. Check out https://kylon.io
AdaL
AdaL is an automation-first agent harness designed to get more done with less of your time. She combines personality, skills, and memory to become a personalized agent that can work alongside you. Check out https://adalagent.ai
Tenki
Tenki provides sandbox environments, cloud compute, and runners for executing code and workloads. It gives builders a place to experiment, run, and scale their work. Check out https://tenki.cloud
Rocket Ride
Rocket Ride helps developers build AI and data pipelines directly in their IDE. It makes it easier to connect data, AI models, processing steps, and outputs into repeatable workflows. Check out https://cloud.rocketride.ai
Prelint
Prelint is your product whisperer, checking every pull request against product specs, business rules, and compliance requirements. It catches spec drift before code ships, turning product decisions into automated checks within your existing GitHub workflow so teams and AI agents can move fast without losing sight of what the product is supposed to do. Check out https://prelint.com
InsForge
InsForge is building agent-native cloud infrastructure for modern AI development. It brings together model gateway, compute, deployment, database, authentication, and more so AI coding agents can operate across the full development workflow. Check out the new product https://www.instacloud.com
Voisekey
Voiskey is an innovative AI voice research team dedicated to Expression Intelligence technology, focusing on the development of next-generation voice interfaces that comprehend a speaker's true intent. Check out https://www.voiskey.ai
Querit
Querit is a real-time search and retrieval API for LLMs and AI products, powered by a trillion-scale multilingual index. It delivers fast, high-precision results with fresh data, configurable recency, and multi-source citations. Check out https://www.querit.ai
Paritok
Paritok drops in and non-destructively compresses tools, files, and history on the fly for longer sessions and smaller bills. Check out https://www.paritok.com
Finch
Finch provides agent skills that give AI agents reusable capabilities for performing specific tasks. Skills can help make agents more useful, structured, and consistent. Check out https://www.finchtech.ai
Thenvoi AI Inc
Thenvoi AI Inc helps AI agents and people work together in a shared environment. Its platform lets agents built with different tools communicate, delegate tasks, and keep context in sync, while giving teams visibility and control over how that work gets done. Check out https://www.band.ai
Glasser
Build AI agents that work with real-world data across your platforms.
Connect, query, and automate data workflows with a single prompt—pay only for what you use. Check out https://glasser.ai/
Apify
Apify is a platform for building, running, and sharing web automation and data extraction tools. It helps developers collect structured data from websites and automate repetitive online tasks. Check out https://apify.com/
Ask the W
Ask the W helps you figure out what is worth building with AI. It helps identify good ideas, tasks that can be handled by agents, places where human judgment is needed, and the next steps to take. Check out https://askthew.com/

About Event

Build Personal AI with Coding Agents
Build Something Personal. Demo What’s Next. 📅
October 7, 2026 · 12:00–6:00 PM
📍 Sports Basement · San Francisco ✨
Build Sprint · Live Demos · Founder & VC Panel · Awards
What would you build if everyone could have their own personal AI?
Join founders, developers, and investors for a hands-on afternoon exploring personal AI—and building it with coding agents.
Start with a live coding-agent demonstration, team up around a real human need, and turn your idea into a working prototype. Then take the stage to demo what you built and join founders and investors for a conversation about what could become a product people use every day.
Come with an idea, join a team, or bring a project you want to take further.
🛠️ PART I · BUILD & DEMO
12:00–4:30 PM | Personal AI Build Challenge
Go from an idea to something you can show. We’ll open with a live demonstration of how coding agents can help you move from a product brief to a working application. Then you’ll form teams and build your own personal AI during a two-hour sprint.
What could you build?
A personal assistant that helps organize your day A learning companion that adapts to your goals
A personal memory tool that helps you find and use your notes
An agent that turns spoken ideas into useful work
A creative companion for writing, brainstorming, or making things
A decision-support tool built around your preferences
Keep it focused: one person, one real need, one working experience.
Use your preferred coding agent to build. Showcase participants and any available sponsored credits will be announced before the event.
Schedule
12:00–12:15 PM · Check-in & Meet Your Fellow Builders Get settled, meet potential teammates, and share what you want to build.
12:15–12:35 PM · Live Coding Agent Demo See how an idea becomes a working prototype—with a practical walkthrough of building, testing, and iterating with a coding agent.
12:35–1:00 PM · Challenge Brief, Team Formation & Setup Choose a use case, define your demo, and get your tools ready.
1:00–3:00 PM · Build Sprint: Build Your Personal AI Two hours to build, test, and refine your prototype.
3:00–3:15 PM · Submit & Reset Submit your project and prepare a short demonstration.
3:15–4:30 PM · Live Demos & Judge Feedback Selected teams demonstrate their prototypes and explain the human need behind them. Demo slots will depend on the number of submissions.
💬 PART II · FROM PROTOTYPE TO PRODUCT
4:30–6:00 PM | Founder & Investor Conversation, Awards & Networking You’ve built a prototype. What would make someone come back tomorrow? After watching the demos, founders and investors will discuss the opportunities emerging in personal AI—and what separates an interesting experiment from a product people trust and use.
Schedule
4:30–5:10 PM · Founder & VC Panel Beyond the Demo: What Makes Personal AI Worth Coming Back To?
A conversation about daily usefulness, memory, personalization, trust, and the path from a small prototype to a consumer business. Panelists will also reflect on ideas demonstrated during the build challenge.
5:10–5:25 PM · Awards & Closing Remarks Recognizing standout projects for usefulness, working execution, and thoughtful personal-AI experiences.
5:25–6:00 PM · Founder, Builder & Investor Networking Try each other’s projects, connect with investors and fellow builders, and find collaborators to keep building with.
Speakers, judges, sponsors, and award details will be announced as confirmed.
✨ About Timing Align with your natural rhythm and discover your personal energy cycles. Visit www.timingai.app/ or get the Timing app on the App Store: apps.apple.com/us/app/timing-spiritual-friend/id6752722833
🎒 What to Bring Bring your laptop, charger, and access to your preferred coding tools. Solo builders and teams are welcome; you can also find teammates on site. For demos, use sample data or information you’re comfortable sharing publicly.
🤝 Who Should Join Developers, startup founders, product designers, and investors interested in personal AI, consumer applications, and building with coding agents. Build something you would use yourself. Show us why someone else would want it too.

About Event

In this 10+ hour intensive hackathon led by the research team at Obvious you will build your autonomous software factory. TLDR: you'll be able to start assigning your agents features to build instead of prompts.
Note: This event is entirely free, including unlimited tokens for the hackathon. Building and tokens will be using an obvious.ai workspace.
We will be awarding over $30K in token prizes to the teams that can build the most in a day!
1st place receives $20,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

2nd place receives $10,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

3rd place receives $5,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

Come alone or come as a team. If you want to valuemaxx this event (and set yourself up to win big) the ideal group to bring is:
a technical founder or engineering leader

a product manager (if you have one)

1+ engineers (the more ai-pilled the better)

What to bring
Your laptop

Access to a real Github repo you care about [or] a clear vision for a greenfield project

A bug backlog or a list of small improvements

We'll set up your Obvious workspace and go through onboarding in-person. Meals and drinks are provided.

10:00 AM – Doors Open
10:30 AM – Opening Session
10:45 AM – Building Begins
1:00 PM – Lunch, with Lightning Talks
3:30 PM – Optional Q&A with Obvious
4:30 PM – Closing Panel
5:00 PM – Awards, Demos & Happy Hour
What you’ll be learning:
How to...
design the complete hands-off build loop

manage a multi-pr autonomous agent swarm

prepare more ambitious builds (entire features or even products)

manage QA, code review, and human feedback without slowing down the work

decide where to spend time vs go hands off

rethink both devops and organizational roles in a world of autonomy

scale autonomous software delivery safely

think about roadmap and software design when you can build anything practical in a day

Obvious is an applied AI research lab with a focus on autonomous product development. We spend our days closing the gap between what's possible and what's doable, treating our own company as the experiment for what it means to operate at agent scale. We've reinvented our product, reshaped our team, accelerated revenue, and 10x'd our shipping velocity in less than a year. At peak velocity we've shipped 1000 PRs in one day with 10 engineers.
Frontier is where we do our best to hand that system to other teams. We're excited to work with you!

About Event

EDIT: This was supposed to be on Oct 3 but is getting delayed because both cohosts are sick :(
Bubble Lab and Lunatechs is happy to present to you guys our 2026 PRE-SF Tech Week event! We know everyone is SUPER excited for tech week so we designed what hopefully will be the PERFECT event to kick it off!
We're bringing this event to you in partnership with the European Startup Embassy, Europe's base in Silicon Valley — a Bay Area hub where European founders land, work, and plug into the US market.

What is Pretty Cool Demos and Pre-Tech Week Social?
First we'll do what we're calling "Pretty Cool Demos!". This will be an open demo sign up list where each person gets 5 minutes to show their demo. Skip the long slow roll dramatic story, just cut to the chase and show us the AMAZING thing you are building! Get to know what each other is doing and help each other connect during Tech Week.
We'll also have a system to share your interests and the Bubble Lab AI system will help us all find potential crew mates! Having a good crew will not only make Tech Week 10x more effective but also make it 10x more enjoyable! We all know that social awkwardness of going to events!
Agenda
6:00pm - Check-in

6:15pm - Introductions - Selina Li and Hanley Leung

6:25pm - Lucky Drop Prize Game - PRIZES TO BE ANNOUNCED!

6:30pm - 5 Minute Demo's Begin

7:00pm - Pre-Tech Week Social w/ AI Matching

7:30pm - Speakers (TBD/OPTIONAL)

8:30pm - Lucky Drop Prize Game #2 - PRIZES TO BE ANNOUNCED!

9:00pm - wrap up

The Demo Lineup So Far!
Hanley - Lucky Drop 3.0 - Battle Royale Prize Game!

Mike Chop - Code.Blue - Making Stroke Obsolete

Matthew Ao - Space (a16z speedrun) - Infinity Space for Computer

Carlo Pizzuti - Rolling Around - making bikepacking easier

Ira Puteri - Legali AI - trauma informed companion for women navigating abuse

Elvin Atwine - Klo - an agentic video editor

Garett Brennan - Epoch Trade - AI quant researcher

Bhanu Kowshik - TBD

Shutian Cheng - TryOffice - Tracking your leads' buying signals

YOU

YOU

YOU

SIGN UP PEOPLE! Let's Go!

Who's this event for?
Founders, Builders, Dreamers, VC and Angels, looking to get some elevator pitch practice, and "looking for crew" for SF Tech Week. No technical level requirements. Just a passion for technology , AI and desire to change the world!
What to Bring?
Yourself, your enthusiasm, your passion, and just be ready to meet great people! Learn, Share, Help, Connect! If you want to give a demo see below on how to add yourself to the list. We'll have an app you can connect to before you arrive, that will be sent to approved attendees.
How to sign up to Demo?
Demo's are totally optional but we highly encourage everyone to sign up. We'll set up the demo line by whoever signs up first and also picking out a few special ones to go first. Please contact HANLEY by:
email info@lunatechs.social

WhatsApp / iMessage: +1 650 4318036

IG: @hanleyleung

And send him the following:
mention: Pretty Cool Demos Event

demo title

one sentence description

URL to slides/demo so ideally we can have it ready for you on our laptop

Any special instructions of extra requirements on the computer such as files to download, logged into what accounts, etc

if you need to use your own computer that's ok too but let us know before hand, we try to minimize computer swapping to keep the pace up

Who Is Bubble Lab?
Bubble Lab (YC W26) is the operating system for paid professional communities — member directory, applications, onboarding, matchmaking and engagement workflows in one place, built around Slack and compatible with Discord, WhatsApp and the rest of your stack. Communities show up juggling ~14 tools and about 20 hours a week of manual admin; Bubble Lab replaces the lot.
It's built by Selina Li and Zach Zhong , a second-time founding duo out of Cornell Tech. Selina went UPenn → quant researcher at J.P. Morgan Asset Management → CEO; Zach went UCSD CS → founding engineer at CutiePet → CTO. Before Bubble Lab they shipped gymii.ai together, an AI nutrition tracker that reached thousands of users through Cornell Tech's Spinouts program. Two people, in San Francisco, out-shipping teams many times their size.

Who is Lunatechs?
A tech-enthusiast community — find your fellow tech lunatics. Talks, workshops, meetups, hackathons; no gatekeeping, no monthly commitment. Born in Hong Kong, now 1,000+ members there, with chapters in Hong Kong and Singapore. After Shanghai the tour hits San Francisco, Dallas, Houston, Los Angeles and Palo Alto — Shanghai gets to open it.
Lunatechs is run by people who've shipped things you've used. Co-founder Hanley Leung is an engineering leader out of Apple, EA and Yahoo!. Co-founder Jason Xu built product at Google and Alibaba. Between them: decades in big tech, and years of hands-on experience working in China's tech world — this isn't a fly-in event; it's a community run by people who know Shanghai's builders are among the best anywhere.

Who is the European Startup Embassy?
"Europe's base in Silicon Valley." A Bay Area hub giving European startups and investors a physical and virtual foothold in the US: coworking and event space, a coliving residence, an online community, and hands-on help with market entry, customer acquisition and raising from US VCs. Led by CEO Vladimira Cincurova.

Venue: European Startup Embassy, 461 Bryant St, San Francisco

Bubble Lab email: hello@bubblelab.ai
Lunatechs www: https://lunatechs.social
Lunatechs email: info@lunatechs.social

About Event

In this 10+ hour intensive hackathon led by the research team at Obvious you will build your autonomous software factory. TLDR: you'll be able to start assigning your agents features to build instead of prompts.
Note: This event is entirely free, including unlimited tokens for the hackathon. Building and tokens will be using an obvious.ai workspace.
We will be awarding over $30K in token prizes to the teams that can build the most in a day!
1st place receives $20,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

2nd place receives $10,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

3rd place receives $5,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

Come alone or come as a team. If you want to valuemaxx this event (and set yourself up to win big) the ideal group to bring is:
a technical founder or engineering leader

a product manager (if you have one)

1+ engineers (the more ai-pilled the better)

What to bring
Your laptop

Access to a real Github repo you care about [or] a clear vision for a greenfield project

A bug backlog or a list of small improvements

We'll set up your Obvious workspace and go through onboarding in-person. Meals and drinks are provided.
Agenda
10:00 AM – Doors Open
10:30 AM – Opening Session
10:45 AM – Building Begins
1:00 PM – Lunch, with Lightning Talks
3:30 PM – Optional Q&A with Obvious
4:30 PM – Closing Panel
5:00 PM – Awards, Demos & Happy Hour
What you’ll be learning:
How to...
design the complete hands-off build loop

manage a multi-pr autonomous agent swarm

prepare more ambitious builds (entire features or even products)

manage QA, code review, and human feedback without slowing down the work

decide where to spend time vs go hands off

rethink both devops and organizational roles in a world of autonomy

scale autonomous software delivery safely

think about roadmap and software design when you can build anything practical in a day

This is for the Engineer & Technical Builder track of our hackathon. If you're interested in learning more about the Product Manager track, check out and register at this Luma: https://luma.com/frontier-builders
What building on the Frontier is like:

-------
About Obvious:
Obvious is an applied AI research lab with a focus on autonomous product development. We spend our days closing the gap between what's possible and what's doable, treating our own company as the experiment for what it means to operate at agent scale. We've reinvented our product, reshaped our team, accelerated revenue, and 10x'd our shipping velocity in less than a year. At peak velocity we've shipped 1000 PRs in one day with 10 engineers.
Frontier is where we do our best to hand that system to other teams. We're excited to work with you!

Request to Join

About Event

Tech Week Prelaunch Event - Physical AI for Anyone | Bring Your Impossible Idea
That product you keep imagining — and quietly talking yourself out of — belongs in the room this Thursday.
You know the one. The idea that shows up in the shower. On the drive home. In that 1 a.m. Notes app draft you never send anyone because… hardware feels too hard, too expensive, too “not for people like me.”
What if that story is wrong?
This Thursday, bring your impossible idea anyway. The wild one. The tender one. The one that makes your friends say “that would be so cool” and then change the subject. We’re building a room where imagination doesn’t get shut down — it gets built.
What it's about
Physical AI for Anyone is 2 hours of creative voltage: founders, dreamers, and first-timers turning something you can only picture in your head into something the physical world can start to hold.
You’ll hear from hardware founders who once stood exactly where you are — scared, excited, unsure — and still shipped something real. Then you’ll open your laptop and chase your idea with Vlight AI: explore how it could look, feel, come apart, get made. Not a lecture. A leap.
There will be laughter. There will be “wait, that actually works?” moments. There will be a one-minute pitch where your idea gets to breathe in front of people who get it. And when you walk out, you won’t just have notes — you’ll have proof that you started.
If you’ve ever felt that little ache of “I wish I could make this,” this night is for that ache.
Who it's for
For the founder with no hardware background and a full heart. For the designer tired of living only on screens. For the student with an impossible sketch. For anyone who’s ever said “someone should invent this” — and secretly meant you.
You don’t need credentials. You need courage for one afternoon. If you can feel the idea, you’re already in.
What you get
Permission to take your impossible idea seriously — in public

A room buzzing with people who want to build, not just talk

Vlight AI credits + humans beside you when you get stuck

Honest stories from 1–2 hardware founders who made the leap

Sixty seconds on stage. A vote. A rush. A winner — and a story you’ll want to tell

Llight snacks, coffee/water/soft drinks, and warmth from Plug and Play That rare high: I didn’t just dream it. I began it.

Guest Judge & Speaker
Jenny Jiang
Co-founder, HarvardXR Summit
AI Product Lead, CVS Health
Jenny will join the pitch session to share feedback and perspectives across AI, product innovation, XR, and emerging technology.
Agenda
3:00pm -3:15pm Networking — find your people, borrow a little bravery

3:15 pm - 3:30pm Kickoff — Hardware founders share how they made the leap

3:15pm - 4:15pm Create with Vlight AI — give your impossible idea a body

4:15pm - 5:00pm 1-min pitch & vote the winner

5:00pm - 6:00pm Founder networking — don’t let the spark cool down alone

What to bring
Laptop + charger

The idea you’ve been protecting (even if it’s messy)

An open heart and a little audacity

Registration
Limited seats. We want a hungry room, not a quiet audience. Request your spot on Luma — we’ll confirm by email. Credits provided. Come with the idea you almost gave up on. Leave a little more dangerous — in the best way.

Plug and Play Sunnyvale Tech Center
Thursday, October 1, 2026 · 3:00–5:00 PM PT
2nd Floor, Silicon Valley Room

Across the series, participants build and pitch new product concepts while meeting people across entrepreneurship, investment, technology, design, culture, and manufacturing.
Promising projects may continue through:
Mentorship

Prototyping exploration

Manufacturing connections

Human Futures Showcase opportunities

Future Human Futures Lab programs and cohort opportunities

Build something real — and discover which ideas are worth continuing.

Join one session or continue building with us throughout the series.

Bring an early product idea, build its first direction with Vlight AI, pitch it in 60 seconds, and receive feedback from our guest judge and fellow builders.
OCT 5 — OFFICIAL LAUNCH
BUILD HUMAN FUTURES
GOOGLE COMMUNITY SPACE · SAN FRANCISCO
The official launch of BUILD HUMAN FUTURES during SF Tech Week.
Our flagship gathering brings together creative talent, founders, investors, technologists, cultural leaders, and guests from San Francisco’s international community.

Mrs. Eleanor Ketter

Build. Pitch. Connect.

PHYSICAL AI BUILD SESSION
The series continues with another hands-on build-and-pitch session connecting creators, founders, technologists, investors, and industry.
Meet people across the startup ecosystem, including VCs, YC alumni founders, experienced entrepreneurs, product leaders, and hardware builders.
Bring an idea. Build it. Pitch it. Find people who may help move it forward.

PHYSICAL AI BUILD SESSION
Our final SF Tech Week session brings together another cross-disciplinary room of founders, designers, technologists, investors, YC alumni, industry leaders, and creative builders.
Build and pitch new ideas, meet potential collaborators, and help identify projects worth continuing beyond Tech Week.
ONE SERIES. FOUR GATHERINGS.
Promising projects from across the series may continue into mentorship, prototyping and manufacturing exploration, Human Futures Showcase opportunities, and future Human Futures Lab programs.

Request to Join

About Event

The VAST Builders Challenge is a three-city technical event series bringing together founders and engineers across New York, London, and San Francisco to build production-ready AI systems.
Spend the day building agents to unlock the value of video. Because video is hard to search and analyze, most of it stays in storage, unwatched and underused.
Experiment with the latest AI infrastructure, collaborate with other ambitious builders, and turn your ideas into shippable prototypes - with access to expert guidance, compute, and the tools you need to ship.
Hosted with VAST Data in collaboration with NVIDIA , SpaceXAI , CoreWeave and Weights & Biases.
Note: Registration closes on September 29th.
Prizes
1st place: NVIDIA DGX Spark™

HuggingFace Microduck

Cursor Credits

Cash Gift Cards

The Builders Stack
Here's what you get out of the box, a lightning-quick setup:
Video understanding: reason over a video clip with NVIDIA Cosmos.

Semantic search: find moments across hours of footage using natural language.

Object detection: real-time detection and tracking across frames with YOLO.

General-purpose LLMs: models from Weights & Biases to power your application logic (e.g. video agents).

The VAST AI OS orchestrates the video ingestion and data layer, models are served on CoreWeave GPUs, and builders ship with Cursor.
Build your own video agent or something no one’s thought of. We'll share the videos to get you started on building video agents.
Judges
Hassan Moustafa - TME, Multimodal AI @ NVIDIA
Adam Ryason, Ph.D. - Product @ NVIDIA
Ram B. - Sr. Developer Advocate @ VAST Data
Brian Verkley - Director, AI Data Platform @ VAST Data
Anushrav V. - Solutions Architect, Physical AI Lead @ CoreWeave
Arnav Verma - Field Engineer @ SpaceXAI
Who should attend
Developers, ML/AI engineers, agent builders, and data engineers, from startups to enterprise teams working with video or multimodal AI.
While individuals are welcome, we encourage teams of up to four members and will prioritize team applications. You can form a team on the day of the event or arrive with one already assembled.
Applications are required. Space is limited. Registration closes one week prior to the event.
Please register using the same email address associated with your Cursor credits. The email you use to register will also be used for the Builders Challenge prerequisites.
Agenda
9:00am Doors Open + Breakfast
9:30am Opening Keynotes
10:00am Build Begins
1:00pm Lunch
5:00pm Demos
7:00pm Closing & Awards
Note: This event will be photographed and filmed. By attending, you consent to appearing in photos and videos that may be used for social media and promotional materials.
All guests must be 18+ and present a valid government-issued physical photo ID at check-in (digital IDs will not be accepted). Scooters and bikes are not permitted in any Amazon building with no on-site parking available.
Sponsors
VAST Data: A unified AI data platform that provides the foundation for managing, processing, and activating data for AI workloads
CoreWeave : AI cloud infrastructure that delivers high-performance GPU compute for training, fine-tuning, and inference workloads.
SpaceXAI : AI-assisted software development tools that help developers move from idea to implementation faster
NVIDIA: Accelerated computing and AI software that enables developers to build and deploy advanced AI applications
Weights & Biases (A CoreWeave company) : AI developer tools for experiment tracking, model evaluation, and collaborative ML development

About Event

AI is moving faster than most security programs can keep up with — agentic tools, MCP servers, and AI-generated code are shipping into production every day, often outrunning the guardrails meant to protect them. This hackathon brings developers and security practitioners together to get hands-on with the skills defining the new discipline of AI Security Engineering. Working in teams, participants will tackle real-world AI security challenges spanning securing MCP servers and agent skills against tool poisoning and supply-chain attacks, and hardening vibe-coded applications.
Whether you're a developer curious about securing AI-powered apps or a security specialist looking to apply your skills to LLMs and agents, you'll leave with practical, portfolio-ready experience — and the kind of muscle memory that only comes from breaking (and fixing) real systems. About Event

The AI Conference Hack Day is where 350 builders unite to do something that was impossible a year ago: build a working product — a real business — in a single day.
This isn't a hackathon in the old sense. No throwaway demos, no clever prototypes that die the next day. The AI Conference Hack Day brings together 350 builders, engineers, product and business minds to ship something real. Something that runs. Something a customers will actually use — and maybe pay for before the day is out.
For one day, the usual excuses disappear. You don't need a team of fifty. You don't need a year of runway. You don't need permission. What used to be a roadmap is now an afternoon. What used to be a funding round is now a focused day of work and the will to ship.
That's not hype. It's where the frontier actually is right now.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei predicts the first billion-dollar company with a single human employee will arrive as soon as 2026 —
Every one of those companies has a day zero. This is where yours could begin.
Here's how it works. You'll have a single day to take an idea from nothing to a working product. You'll build alongside the sharpest practitioners in applied AI — the engineers, ML leads, and founders who already live at the edge of what these tools can do. Mentors will be in the room. The energy will be unlike anything else at the conference. And at the end of the day, prizes go to the teams who didn't just build something interesting, but built something real.
The top prize is the one that matters most. The best product team won't just take home recognition — they'll take the main stage at The AI Conference the very next day to pitch a panel of top venture capitalists. That's the kind of room most founders wait years to get into. You could earn your seat in twenty-four hours.
This is the bet we're making: that the next great company won't be announced in a press release. It'll be built in a room full of people who decided not to wait. It'll start as a half-formed idea on Day ZERØ and walk out as something real.
The era of the solo builder, the tiny team that punches a hundred times above its weight, the one-person company — it's not coming someday. It's starting now, and it's starting here.
This is your shot.
Don't miss it.

Stanford, CA

Registration

Welcome! To join the event, please register below.
Register

About Event

Build open agents that work together

The Collaborative Agent Hackathon is a one-day event for building open-source, collaborative AI agents with Flower .
Agents are changing what’s possible. We’ll explore how they can achieve more by working together safely in human-supervised multi-agent teams.
You’ll form a team on the day, build a working prototype, and demo it at the end of the event. Projects can range from simple agent collaborations to more complex systems that delegate tasks, share context, and coordinate their work.
You don’t need an existing team or a fully developed idea. Bring your laptop, your interests, and a willingness to collaborate.

The event is generously supported by Nebius , which is providing all compute resources for the hackathon, sending expert technical mentors and judges, and contributing to the prize pool.
The hackathon challenge
Build an open-source agent or multi-agent system with Flower that puts safe, human-supervised collaboration at the heart of the solution.
Your project could bring agents together to:
Automate a real-world task

Form self-improving loops through feedback and iteration

Work across distributed machines and datasets

Flower simplifies building multi-agent systems, with support for distributed coordination, collaborative learning and inference, and privacy-aware deployment. It is built with an open-source community of more than 7,000 users worldwide.

Projects from all industries and application areas are welcome — including scientific research, healthcare, finance, content/media production, education, public services, software development and entirely new forms of human-agent collaboration.
Team formation
Participants register individually.
Teams of two to four people will be formed during the morning, unless formed earlier . The organisers will help participants find teammates with complementary interests and experience.
Already know your team? Please provide your teammates’ names when registering.
Bringing an idea is optional.
Eligibility: Everyone is welcome, including builders from startups and companies, as well as students, researchers, and postdocs from all universities.
Awards and judges
Teams will compete for a prize pool worth more than US$5,000 , with awards presented after the final demos to recognize outstanding projects.
Judges include:
Anastasia Raskolova (Nebius)

Disha Patil (ARM)

Daniel Nata Nugraha (Flower Labs)

Naveen Purushotham (AMD)

Daria Balashova (Nebius)

Dimitris Stripelis (Flower Labs)

Mehul Vani (Nvidia)

Sai Nagabhairava (Meta)

Special thanks to our sponsor Nebius for contributing to the prize pool, providing all compute resources for the hackathon, and bringing expert technical mentors and judges.
Further details on prizes will be shared before the event.

Schedule
9:30–10:00 — Opening, check-in and breakfast
Meet other participants and share your interests and experience.
10:00–10:15 — Welcome
Introduction to the event, the challenge and the day’s practical arrangements.
10:15–10:45 — Collaborative agents with Flower
A technical introduction covering collaborative agent architectures, safe coordination, self-improvement loops and the available Flower resources.
10:45–11:00 — Team formation
Meet potential collaborators and form teams of two to four, unless your team was formed earlier.
11:00–12:45 — Build session
Define the project, design the agent interactions and begin implementation.
12:45–1:30 — Lunch
1:30–5:15 — Build session
Develop and test the system, refine the collaboration or self-improvement loop and prepare the demonstration. Mentors will be available throughout.
5:15–5:30 — Demo preparation
5:30–6:45 — Project demonstrations
Teams present their projects, followed by brief questions.
6:45–7:30 — Dinner, awards and closing remarks
Enjoy dinner as we celebrate the winning projects and bring the hackathon to a close.

You bring the idea. Build the AI that makes it happen.
The Challenge
Build Your AI Co-Founder is a hackathon where you build and ship a company with a founding team of 2–4 co-founders, combining humans and AI.
Every team must have at least one human and one AI co-founder. You decide the rest—including who takes which role, what you build, and how your founding team works together.
AI co-founders can take any role: CEO, CTO, Product, Marketing, Sales, Research, or anything your company needs.
The goal is to experience what it means to build a real company with AI as part of the founding team—from idea to execution to a shipped product.
Prizes
Build the Product challenge using AdaL prize: +1 month AdaL pro for the winners
Using AdaL, build and ship a functional app or MVP for a real-world problem. Your product should be something real people can use and should demonstrate how your human–AI founding team turns an idea into a working company.
The focus is on execution: build a useful product, validate it with real users, and show what your AI co-founder contributed to the journey from idea to launch.
Ask The W think Before You Build Challenge: Prizes: Gift cards for best context, most bugs found and an opportunity to build with the founder. More details: https://askthew.com/hackathon

The fastest way to ship is to avoid building the wrong thing.

Use Ask The W to gather the right context, question assumptions and get clear on what should be built before writing code. Understand first. Build second.
Tenki code review challenge: 1000 Tenki credits for winner
Use Tenki to sandbox, test, and review your project’s code. Identify bugs and issues in AI-generated code, improve the implementation, and demonstrate how your team builds, reviews, fixes, and ships reliable software.

Our sponsors provide the technology and infrastructure you'll use to turn your ideas into working companies.
AdaL

Nebius
Nebius provides AI-focused cloud infrastructure and computing resources designed to help teams build, train, and run modern AI applications and workloads.
Tenki

Aisa

Prepare your company to raise funding. Your AI co-founder researches investors, finds the right fit, builds fundraising materials, and helps manage outreach.

Grow It: Acquire Users
Build a repeatable growth engine. Your AI co-founder helps define your audience, develop positioning, test channels, run experiments, and measure results.
Make It: Build the Product
Turn an idea or problem into a working product. Your AI co-founder helps validate the problem, define the MVP, design the experience, build, test, and iterate.
Run It: Operate the Business
Make your business run better. Your AI co-founder helps improve processes across scheduling, customers, team coordination, reporting, inventory, and automation.

structuredEvent.name: Build Your AI Co-Founder Hackathon
structuredEvent.description:
If you have registered on here, please join discord channel as well: discord.gg/Ku3GdmbUx7
You bring the idea. Build the AI that makes it happen.
The Challenge
Build Your AI Co-Founder is a hackathon where you build and ship a company with a founding team of 2–4 co-founders, combining humans and AI.
Every team must have at least one human and one AI co-founder. You decide the rest—including who takes which role, what you build, and how your founding team works together.
AI co-founders can take any role: CEO, CTO, Product, Marketing, Sales, Research, or anything your company needs.
The goal is to experience what it means to build a real company with AI as part of the founding team—from idea to execution to a shipped product.
Prizes
Build the Product challenge using AdaL prize: +1 month AdaL pro for the winners
Using AdaL, build and ship a functional app or MVP for a real-world problem. Your product should be something real people can use and should demonstrate how your human–AI founding team turns an idea into a working company.
The focus is on execution: build a useful product, validate it with real users, and show what your AI co-founder contributed to the journey from idea to launch.
Ask The W think Before You Build Challenge: Prizes: Gift cards for best context, most bugs found and an opportunity to build with the founder. More details: https://askthew.com/hackathon

The fastest way to ship is to avoid building the wrong thing.

Use Ask The W to gather the right context, question assumptions and get clear on what should be built before writing code. Understand first. Build second.
Tenki code review challenge: 1000 Tenki credits for winner
Use Tenki to sandbox, test, and review your project’s code. Identify bugs and issues in AI-generated code, improve the implementation, and demonstrate how your team builds, reviews, fixes, and ships reliable software.
Sponsors & Tools
Our sponsors provide the technology and infrastructure you'll use to turn your ideas into working companies.
AdaL
AdaL is automation-first agent harness and coding companion. While any coding agent can build, AdaL uniquely turns your codebase into go-to-market execution, helping you ship faster from development to launch.. Learn more at adalagent.ai.
Nebius
Nebius provides AI-focused cloud infrastructure and computing resources designed to help teams build, train, and run modern AI applications and workloads.
Tenki
Tenki provides developer infrastructure at tenki.cloud, including sandboxes, code review, and code runners to help teams safely build, test, and iterate on their products.

Aisa
100+ AI models, composable skills, and deployable agents unified under one API. Build, monetize, and scale autonomous workflows with pay-per-call simplicity at Aisa.com
Ask the W
Ask the W helps you figure out what is worth building with AI. It helps identify good ideas, tasks that can be handled by agents, places where human judgment is needed, and the next steps to take.
Venue and Community Partner
AI Global Campus
Global Platform for Applied &Agentic AI AI for Humanity. AI with Education. AI Beyond Systems

Sartorial
Sartorial helps make products more intelligently discoverable and recommendable.
Articuler AI
Articuler.ai helps people find the right professionals for their goals — whether that's raising a round, finding a co-founder, or entering a new market
Bridge US
Bridge US is an AI-powered networking platform for conferences and events. It helps attendees find the right customers, partners, engineers, investors, and other connections
Devnovate
Hosts hackathons and events all over the world

Hosted by Crewbase Collective
Crewbase Collective is organization running hackathons and events across the San Francisco
Schedule
Before 12:00 PM: Online hacking begins
12:00 PM – 1:00 PM: Welcome session
1:00 PM – 6:00 PM: Hacking continues
6:00 PM – 7:00 PM: Judging
7:00 PM – 8:00 PM: Finalist demos and winner announcements
8:00 PM – 10:00 PM: Networking
Participants who are unable to attend the venue can participate and hack online throughout the event.
Judges & Mentors
Merve Isler: Fouder @ Marvelous & AI Insiders
Ash Bao: Head of Marketing @ Gruve
Julie Zhu: Head of Design @ Zawa (Meitu)
Anya Ozmen: Founder @ Gameer
Vince Kohli: Strategic Advisor @ GoogleDeepmind
Sumit Jagdale: Founder @ Sartorial
Saurabh Khire: Software Engineer @ Govia
David Li: Co-Founder @ Induction Labs
Mia Yang: AI Product Manager @ Baidu USA
Ali Amjed: Research Fellow @ R42 Group
Optional Tracks
Build It: Launch the Business
Turn your idea into a launch-ready business. Your AI co-founder helps with research, permits, costs, suppliers, branding, operations, and the launch plan.
Fund It: Raise Capital
Prepare your company to raise funding. Your AI co-founder researches investors, finds the right fit, builds fundraising materials, and helps manage outreach.
Sell It: Get Customers
Get your first customers. Your AI co-founder identifies prospects, researches them, creates personalized outreach, and supports the sales process.
Grow It: Acquire Users
Build a repeatable growth engine. Your AI co-founder helps define your audience, develop positioning, test channels, run experiments, and measure results.
Make It: Build the Product
Turn an idea or problem into a working product. Your AI co-founder helps validate the problem, define the MVP, design the experience, build, test, and iterate.
Run It: Operate the Business
Make your business run better. Your AI co-founder helps improve processes across scheduling, customers, team coordination, reporting, inventory, and automation.
Choose your own
How It Comes Together
The company is up to you. The co-founders are up to you. The roles are up to you. The track defines what you want to accomplish. For example:
Company is AI bookkeeping platform. Co-founders are Human CEO + Human CTO + AI Product + AI Sales
Track is Sell It. Build the product, find potential customers, run outreach, and aim to secure the first paying customers.
Company is AI travel startup. Co-founders are Human Product Lead + AI CEO + AI Growth. Track is Grow It. Build the product, define the target audience, launch growth experiments, and acquire the first users.
Company is Developer productivity tool. Co-founders are Human CTO + AI Product + AI Marketing. Track is Make It. Validate the problem, build the MVP, test it with developers, and ship a working product.
Choose your company. Build your founding team. Pick your mission. Then go build.

Same deliverables as in-person participants

Prize pool: $5K in GCP credits

VC pitch access for top submissions

Build with Gemini, ship a prototype, post your demo, and let your network do the talking. Top submissions get 30-minute meetings with funds.
📋 Submission Requirements
All projects must use the Google Gemini model. Each team must submit the following by 2:30 PM sharp:
One-Pager for the team — Short plain text describing your team and your pedigree

One-Pager for the idea — Short plain text describing your idea and prototype

Hosted Prototype — Working demo link (via Google AI Studio & Google Cloud Run)

2-Minute Video — Team introduction and elevator pitch

1-Minute Video — Prototype demo (Playcast)

Code Repository — Link via Google AI Studio sharing

Data Usage & Judging Consent: By submitting your prototype Playcast, you authorize organizers to use your submission in paid social ads (e.g., Facebook). Real-world performance metrics (CPM, CTR, CPC, etc.) will be collected and used as core market validation data for Phase 2 (post-event) judging. You may opt out by notifying organizers prior to submission; data sharing with sponsors and investors is a condition of participation.

Technical Feasibility — Does it actually work?

Innovation & Novelty — Is the approach creative or clever?

Real-World Applicability — Would people genuinely use it?

Market Potential & Fundability — Could this become venture-backable?

Go-to-Market Traction — Social engagement on your demo video (likes, shares, views)

Social Engagement Component: Your demo YouTube video must be shared publicly. Engagement counts toward your score:
Phase 1 — Tracked during the hackathon (5:00 PM cutoff)

Phase 2 — Continued tracking for 2 weeks post-event (viral reach + Playcast metrics)

🎯 Competition Format
Semi-Finals: All submissions undergo asynchronous review by the judging panel.

Finals: Top teams advance to live presentations — 10 minutes per team (5-min pitch + 5-min Q&A) on stage before the full panel of VCs and special guests. Winners announced at 5:30 PM.

Can I pitch an existing startup? Absolutely! If you win, you can pitch either your hackathon project or your existing company during the 30-minute VC meetings.
What's the team size limit? Up to 5 people.
Can I participate solo? Yes.
Can I participate remotely? Yes! The Online Track has the same deliverables, with submissions due by end of day, September 27. No live streaming — judging is based on 7-day social engagement (Phase 2 conditions). The Online Track has a $5K GCP credits prize pool.
When do VC meetings happen? Winners will schedule 30-minute pitch meetings with selected funds after the event.
What should I bring? Laptop, charger, and your best ideas!
📌 Age Requirement
This event is open to participants 18 years and older. Valid ID may be required for check-in.

To make sure you're ready to compete in our main Google DeepMind track, please take a few minutes to complete the prerequisite assignment/tutorial below.
What to do
Spend 5–10 minutes creating a simple prototype in AI Studio.

Submit it through the provided Google Form.

This confirms that:
You're familiar with the platform

Your GCP billing account is enabled

Tutorial: https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/getting-started-with-gemini-3-deploy-your-first-gemini-3-app-to-google-cloud-run

Submit your test app: Open Google Form

Deadline: Saturday at 9:00 AM PST
Thank you!

As developers rely heavily on AI to write code at unprecedented speeds, Snyk continuously scans and secures application code, open-source dependencies, containers, and cloud environments right within the developer’s workflow. Build Your First App with AI 🚀
Hands-on AI + Hardware Workshop · Ages 12–18
📍 October 4, 2026 · Silkroad Innovation Hub, Menlo Park
Hosted by NextGen Initiative, Silicon Valley in partnership with Silkroad Innovation Hub
Sponsored by Vostok & Shawarma
Come with an idea. Leave with your first prototype—and a path to keep building.
Create a study planner, a game, a tool for your school club, or explore a smart-device prototype. You’ll try vibe coding: describing your idea in plain language, using AI to help write the code, then testing and improving what you build.
Learn directly from Dara Tumenbayeva , —a former Amazon software engineer, former software engineer and data scientist at SEEK Asia , and founder building Aora . With experience across 30+ hackathons and hackathon judging, Dara will help you turn a big idea into an achievable project and a confident demo. Meet Dara .
You’ll learn to:
Build with AI using accessible tools and available free tiers.

Test your creation , spot mistakes, and use AI responsibly.

Demo your project and start documenting it for a portfolio you can develop for university applications, competitions, and future opportunities.

Best projects gets to raise mind controlled drone and more cool prizes !
AI brings enormous opportunities and serious responsibilities. Learning to build with it—and question its output—is a skill you can start developing now.
This workshop is the first step toward a planned ongoing NextGen program , where students can keep improving their projects and learning together.
No coding experience needed. Bring a laptop, charger, and curiosity.
Tool access depends on age and platform eligibility; younger participants will need an appropriate adult-led setup.
Learn. Build. Create. Share.

About Event

AI Commerce Gallery — ZooWork × AI Valley
What does the next generation of AI-powered commerce look like?
ZooWork and AI Valley are bringing together builders, founders, engineers, designers, and commerce leaders for AI Commerce Gallery — a curated one-day hackathon and interactive showcase for products pushing commerce forward.
On October 3rd, AI Commerce Gallery takes over The Walt Disney Family Museum in San Francisco for a full day of building, demos, and exploration.
Teams will build throughout the day in the Diane Disney Miller Exhibition Hall before the evening program moves into the Main Museum, with presentations in the Theater and Lower Lobby and private access to the Museum’s Main Galleries from 7:30–9 PM.

Teams will build AI-powered products across:
E-commerce & storefront experiences

Merchant operations, inventory, fulfillment & payments

Restaurants, retail, POS & physical commerce

AI agents, MCP integrations & workflow automation

The strongest projects will take the stage in The Walt Disney Family Museum’s Theater , bringing a day of bold ideas to life in a place built to celebrate imagination.
Then celebrate the winners, meet fellow builders, and enjoy private access to the Museum’s Main Galleries from 6–9 PM — ending the day with a little Disney magic.

Best Use of ZooWork
People’s Choice

Come build — or come see — what the next generation of AI-powered commerce looks like.
ZooWork — The AI agent delivery platform for FDEs and domain experts. Build, deploy, and deliver production-ready AI agents to your team or clients in minutes—with Agent Builder, Agent Runtime, model gateway, data, and integrations all in one place. ZooWork turns your expertise into repeatable AI solutions that run inside real business operations, connected to the tools your teams already use. Learn more at zoowork.ai .

Moss ( moss.dev ) is a real-time semantic search engine that gives AI agents sub-10ms retrieval without the latency and infrastructure overhead of traditional vector databases.

Entire is building the next agentic Git forge. Store your prompts, output, tool calls, and more alongside your code in Git, perform rapid-fast Git operations on their distributed Git network, and save token usage on their human-agent developer platform.

Tavily helps AI agents access up-to-date information from the web. Its search, extraction, and crawling APIs let developers build applications that research topics, gather data, and turn web content into useful answers.

Novita AI is an AI infrastructure platform for builders. It offers access to AI models through a single API, along with GPU compute for training and inference and secure runtimes for AI agents. Developers can start with serverless APIs and scale to dedicated endpoints or GPU clusters as their needs grow.

BAND helps AI agents and people work together in a shared environment. Its platform lets agents built with different tools communicate, delegate tasks, and keep context in sync, while giving teams visibility and control over how that work gets done.

AI Valley is a community rooted in supporting exceptional first generation builders, founders, and creators. We curate environments where ambitious people meet collaborators, mentors, and opportunities through hackathons, workshops, and intimate gatherings across AI, tech, and the arts. If you care about who you build with as much as what you build, this is your place.

Moss (moss.dev) is a real-time semantic search engine that gives AI agents sub-10ms retrieval without the latency and infrastructure overhead of traditional vector databases.

Entire is building the next agentic Git forge. Store your prompts, output, tool calls, and more alongside your code in Git, perform rapid-fast Git operations on their distributed Git network, and save token usage on their human-agent developer platform. 

Tavily helps AI agents access up-to-date information from the web. Its search, extraction, and crawling APIs let developers build applications that research topics, gather data, and turn web content into useful answers.

Novita AI is an AI infrastructure platform for builders. It offers access to AI models through a single API, along with GPU compute for training and inference and secure runtimes for AI agents. Developers can start with serverless APIs and scale to dedicated endpoints or GPU clusters as their needs grow.

About Event

Mission Applied: Maritime Dual-Use Announcement Mixer
Mission Applied is the new partnership between Berkeley Gateway Accelerator and the Berkeley Institute for Security and Governance (BISG). BISG does the policy and translation work: analysis, recommendations, convening. Mission Applied is the action arm, the piece that takes capability out of the labs and classrooms and turns it into companies and scalable solutions. If you've got a concept, a research thread, or a company in national security or dual-use tech, this is who you want to know.
Our first move: bringing Fincantieri's engineering challenges to Berkeley.

The evening

An informal mixer at BGA. Food, drinks, and a room full of people working on hard problems in defense and dual-use tech.

You'll hear from Mission Applied on what we're doing and where we're headed, from Mind the Bridge and Fincantieri on the October hackathon, and from mentors and judges pulled from the defense innovation ecosystem, including active-duty Navy leadership working on emerging tech acquisition.

Then we'll get out of the way and let you talk to each other.

The hackathon we're announcing

Fincantieri Maritime Dual-Use Hackathon, October 16-18 in San Francisco. Fincantieri builds the Italian Navy's submarines, the world's largest cruise ships, and the US Coast Guard's Constellation-class frigates. Their engineers wrote the problem statements themselves.

Three tracks: OT Cybersecurity & Blast Radius Analysis, Piping Layout Optimization, and Software-Defined Vessel. Qualcomm and Arduino hardware on hand. Standout concepts get mentorship from Fincantieri's expert network and a real path toward application inside the company.

We'll walk through the tracks, the hardware, and what a strong team looks like, so you show up in October ready to build instead of ready to read.

Who should be here

Students, founders, engineers, researchers, and anyone curious about where deep tech meets national security. Undergrads and grad students from across campus, plus NPS, UCSD, and the community colleges around the East Bay. No maritime background required.

Come solo or bring your team.

Hosted by Mission Applied: Berkeley Gateway Accelerator × Berkeley Institute for Security and Governance, with Mind the Bridge and Fincantieri.
Sign-up here to register: https://luma.com/mvcg9eyw

About Event

“I have to be on <platform> because that’s where everyone already is.”
That’s the power of network effects, and the fiction that big tech monopolies rely on. But challenging this doesn’t have to mean convincing everyone to move at once.
You don’t have to build the next social network. Just something one other person would choose to use with you.
Join us for a night of building small, personal alternatives to the platforms we feel stuck with. Start with one connection—a friend, a collaborator, your group chat, or someone you meet tonight. What could you make that brings something useful, personal, or unexpectedly delightful to both sides?
Some starting points:
A private messaging app built around your group’s quirks.

A stablecoin-based way to split rent or settle up with friends across borders.

A friends-only collection of travel recommendations

A better way to find your people during Tech Week—and stay connected afterward.

A place to share what you’re making that optimizes for connection, not eyeballs.

Come brainstorm ideas from hearing how other people live and work, build and demo a prototype, and get inspired by seeing what others have made. Work solo or team up. Bring an idea, or find one here.
SCHEDULE:
Doors close at 6:45 (BUT we fixed the intercom this time so buzz and we'll let you up)
6pm - 6:30pm — meet people, brainstorm ideas, grab food.
6:30pm — kickoff. Some quick words.
6:30 - 9:00pm — quiet time, work solo or in groups.
9:00 - 9:30pm — demos. We'll open up first to projects built today, then to work built on top of preexisting projects. Submit your projects by pushing to github and adding the topic tag #punksoftware.
9:30pm - 10pm — Try out other folks' projects and ask them questions about how they built it!

---

This is #9 in our punk software hack night series, a biweekly evening event bringing together creators of varied backgrounds to work on projects that dismantle entrenched power structures.
Punk software can loosely be defined as: "software they (big tech monopolists) would never build"; or "software which stands against lock-in, walled gardens, and other forms of user capture".
---
Imbue is an AI company building software that belongs to you. We’re building toward an open agent ecosystem where you can understand, modify, and verify AI agents, so they only work in your interest. Learn about our work and what we stand for: www.imbue.com or / imbue_ai .

This event is a part of #SFTechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com .

Five to six short, live demos

Original Jev variants and real-world applications

Honest breakdowns of what worked and what broke

Lessons about latency, cost, confidence, training, and implementation

Good food (dumpling bar), drinks, and plenty of time to meet other builders

An optional open-demo period after the talks

As a Hugging Face partner, we host one of the largest collections of open-source models with 12,000+ models deployed, working to make state-of-the-art AI more accessible.
TinyFish is building the infrastructure for agents to reliably interact with the live web, navigating websites, executing multi-step workflows, and returning structured results. We offer search, fetch, and agent capabilities.

About Event

What’s actually working for AI products right now?
Hosted by Catalyst Bay , AScaleX , and Brex
Most AI events are vendors talking about their own product. This one is the people responsible for growth at AI companies talking about what actually moved numbers.
A panel, a round table, and a long happy hour. 80 people · 40 founders + 40 GTM leaders , so you will actually talk to everyone.
The panel: Going to market when the category is contested, and nobody has won it yet. How to find demand before you have anything to sell. What positioning survives contact with real buyers. How to pick first customers for distribution rather than revenue.
Speakers :
Ravish Agrawal, Head of Growth Marketing, Gamma - Ravish leads growth marketing at Gamma. Before Gamma he spent five years as co-founder and CEO of Able, a VC-backed edtech app that grew to three million users before he exited.

Mada Seghete, Co-founder, Upside - Mada is the co-founder and CEO of Upside, a revenue attribution and intelligence platform for B2B companies. Before that, she co-founded Branch and built Mobile Growth, a community of 22,000+ mobile marketers and app developers. She co-hosts the Future of Marketing podcast.

Juliana Chyzhova, Head of Marketing, AGI, Inc.

The round tables: An open conversation around the GTM challenges people in the room are working through right now. Bring a question, compare approaches, and hear how other founders and operators are thinking about demand, positioning, customers, and distribution.
Happy hour: Food and drinks, and the part of the evening where the useful conversations happen.
Who this is for
GTM leads and heads of growth at AI companies

Founders still running go-to-market themselves

First marketing and sales hires at AI startups

Investors who spend their time on portfolio distribution

What you leave with: A positioning read on your own product from people who have done it. Two or three tactics you can run next week. And a short list of people worth following up with.

About Event

Bring one broken agent problem. Leave with the next fix.
Your agent worked in the demo. Then production introduced messy context, unreliable tools, strange edge cases, and real users.
Fix My Agent is a hands-on AI agent clinic for builders with a real problem to solve. Bring an agent, MCP server, workflow, or even a failure you can describe—we’ll help you diagnose the highest-leverage next fix.
You’ll get practical help with:
Tool-call and MCP reliability

Agent evaluation and testing

Debugging brittle workflows and bad outputs

Observability, production failures, and deployment

Turning a promising demo into something people can use

How it works
Arrive with one agent problem, workflow, or use case.

Meet with builders and developer-tool experts at focused clinic stations.

Leave with a clear diagnosis and next-step plan.

Share fixes and lessons with the room during a short live wrap-up.

You don’t need a polished demo or code you can share. A real use case, starter workflow, screenshots, logs, or a stubborn question is enough.
Best for: engineers, technical founders, AI product builders, and teams actively building with agents or MCP.
Space is intentionally limited so everyone can get meaningful hands-on help. Registration is reviewed to keep the room useful for everyone.
Hosted with AI Valley, PostHog, GMI Cloud, MCPJam, Arcade.dev, and CodeRabbit.

About Event

Jev is a new kind of model from TypeSafe AI. It takes unstructured context and returns typed, probabilistic decisions that software can act on.
Using Jev well changes how you design workflows. You have to decide which judgments belong to the model, how to frame those decisions, and when the result should trigger an action, human review, or escalation. The fastest way to develop that instinct, or understand the “Jevability” of a problem, is to build.
Join us at the PromptQL office on Tuesday, September 29, from 4–7 p.m. PT for a hands-on evening exploring what becomes possible when decisions get fast, structured, and cheap.
We’ll start with a lightning session dissecting the architecture of four or five real systems built with Jev, and show off some of the best builds from the previous session. We’ll look at patterns such as routing work, selecting from existing options, ranking evidence, verifying agent output, and turning confidence into reliable control flow.
Then we’ll hack.
Bring a workflow, product idea, or recurring judgment you want to rebuild. You’ll leave with a working prototype, a sharper sense of where Jev fits, and practical patterns you can reuse in future systems.
Schedule
4:00 PM: Doors open and introductions
4:15 PM: Jev architecture lightning talks
5:00 PM: Hackathon
6:30 PM: Demos and discussion
7:00 PM: Wrap
No Jev or app-building experience is needed. Engineers, founders, product builders, and anyone curious about decision-driven automation are welcome.
This is a small, hands-on gathering hosted by PromptQL. Come ready to build. Dinner will be provided.
